title: near, lookAt and OrbitControls
sub: How not to clip nearby objects, and how to let users orbit the scene
cards/0/task: The red cube is right next to the camera, but you cannot see it. Fix it.
cards/1/body:
Each pixel's depth is stored with limited precision, and almost all of it is spent on the area close to near. Make near too small and distant surfaces start to flicker, showing through each other. This is z-fighting.

The rule: near as large as possible, far as small as possible, as long as the scene still fits.
cards/2/q: Distant walls flicker and "bleed" through each other. What do you check first?
cards/2/options/0: Whether near is too small (and far too large)
cards/2/explain: The classic cause of z-fighting is near = 0.0001 with far = 100000.
cards/3/task: The blue cube should NOT be drawn (it is background and just gets in the way), but red and green should.
cards/4/body: You can put the camera anywhere and turn it toward a point: camera.lookAt(x, y, z).
cards/5/title: OrbitControls: spin it with the mouse
cards/5/body: A ready-made add-on: dragging orbits the camera around a target, the wheel zooms. With enableDamping the motion is smooth, and then you need controls.update() in the loop.
cards/6/q: You turned on enableDamping and the camera jerks around. Before which line does controls.update() belong?
cards/6/explain: controls.update() goes before render. It is what produces the smooth easing.
cards/7/pairs/3/1: Turn the camera toward a point
cards/8/explain: three/addons/ is the short path to the examples and add-ons shipped in the three package.
